data.answer:
**Yes—if it is not renewed.** A registered trade mark is protected for 10 years and must be renewed every 10 years to remain registered.[1]

There is no fixed maximum lifespan: a trade mark can be renewed in perpetuity, so long as it is in use.[2]

citations.quote: Registered trade marks are afforded protection for 10 years.
To remain registered, a registered trade mark must be renewed every 10 years.

claims.text: A registered trade mark is protected for 10 years and must be renewed every 10 years to remain registered; otherwise its registration expires.

citations.quote: Trade marks can be renewed every 10 years in perpetuity so long as they are in use

claims.text: A trade mark has no fixed maximum lifespan and can be renewed in perpetuity so long as it is in use.
